newsitem.title: POLAND: ZLoty dives lower as more floods approach.
newsitem.headline: ZLoty dives lower as more floods approach.

text.p: The Polish zloty fell nearly one percentage point at bid in early Thursday trade on news that more rains and floods may hit southern and western Poland over the next several days, dealers said.
They said foreign and domestic specuative selling would continue as long as the economic effects of the recent flooding were not clear, placing the zloty under downward pressure.

"In the next several days the zloty should stabilise between -2.5 to -3.0 percent from parity but a second wave of floods is coming, so the zloty could fall before flattening out," said Jaroslaw Dryjski, dealer at Bank Slaski SA.
Others said however that the zloty would likely trade between three and five percent below the parity rate in the near-term without much impetus to make up recently lost ground.
At 0900 GMT the zloty was 3.48/4.09 percent below the parity against opening's at -2.53/-4.04 percent. A week earlier it traded at around 0.6 percent above the parity rate.
It was at 3.4900/5100 to the dollar, against opening's 3.4450/950 and at 1.9370/490 to the mark, against 1.9285/575.
Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz told parliament this morning that weather forecasts showed heavy rain overnight may cause a new wave of floods in the country's south.
The nervous and relatively shallow local forex market brushed aside Finance Minister Marek Belka's statement that the downward trend on the zloty would soon reverse.
"Belka's talking up the zloty didn't have any effect on the market," one dealer said.
Dealers said foreign investor withdrawal from Poland would continue to put the zloty under downward pressure.

"Poland has lost most of its longer-term (T-bond) investors and one can only expect short-term capital inflows and speculation on the zloty for at least the next six months," said Wojciech Kowalczyk, senior dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.

On the money market rates slipped in early trade as some liquidity was found in the near-term, but longer deposits remained on higher ground signalling that the market expected the market to stay tight for some time.
"This week's one-day rate rise fever has subsided, but longer deposit rates could stay high longer," a dealer said.

At 0930 GMT Overnight rates were at 23.02/23.50 percent against opening's 23.65/23.85 and tomorrow/next rates were at 23.03/23.64 percent against 23.70/23.90. One month deposits were quoted at 23.44/24.15 percent.
